record.paper_title: Lower Bounds for Unrestricted Boolean Circuits: Open Problems
record.original_question: Is there a non-gate-elimination method for proving lower bounds for unrestricted Boolean circuits that can be extended past the current 2n barrier?

evidence.quote: Are there approaches other than gate elimination for proving lower bounds for unrestricted circuits.
Can any of these non-gate-elimination methods be extended to get stronger than 2n lower bounds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Boolean circuits over the full binary basis B₂ (the set of all binary Boolean functions), where the size of a circuit is the number of gates and the input variables x₁,…,xₙ are not counted. The "gate-elimination" method is the standard inductive technique used to prove lower bounds on the size of such circuits: one fixes a small number of input variables of an alleged minimal circuit so as to force the elimination of several gates, and then applies an inductive hypothesis to the resulting smaller circuit. All current proofs of linear lower bounds of the form cn − o(n) on the B₂-circuit size of an explicit Boolean function f : {0,1}ⁿ → {0,1} (including the strongest known constants c slightly above 3) are obtained via this gate-elimination paradigm. The paradigm itself is known to be incapable of yielding lower bounds of the form 5n or larger.

Question: Is there a method other than gate elimination — i.e., a fundamentally different proof technique — that proves a lower bound of the form cn for the B₂-circuit size of some explicit family of Boolean functions, with constant c strictly greater than 2, and which can in principle be pushed beyond the 2n barrier that is currently the best achievable by known non-gate-elimination techniques?
artifact.status_search_result: As of 2026, all known strong linear lower bounds for unrestricted B₂-circuits (the strongest being 3.1n − o(n) by Li and Yang, 2022) still rely on the gate-elimination technique. Known non-gate-elimination methods (e.g., the OR-of-CNFs decomposition by Golovnev–Kulikov and related approaches) have not been pushed beyond the 2n barrier. No technique other than gate elimination has produced a super-2n lower bound for explicit functions.

status_evidence.title: 3.1n − o(n) circuit lower bounds for explicit functions (STOC 2022)
status_evidence.snippet: The strongest known lower bound 3.1n − o(n) is obtained via gate elimination.
status_evidence.claim: Best current bound (3.1n) still uses gate elimination.

status_evidence.title: Convergent Gate Elimination and Constructive Circuit Lower Bounds (arXiv:2602.17942)
status_evidence.snippet: Gate elimination is the only method known that can prove complexity lower bounds for explicit functions against unrestricted Boolean circuits.
status_evidence.claim: Gate elimination remains the only method giving strong explicit lower bounds as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Circuit Depth Reductions (Golovnev–Kulikov, ECCC 2018)
status_evidence.snippet: Suggests a non-gate-elimination approach expressing circuits of size s as OR of 2^{s/3.9} 16-CNFs.
status_evidence.claim: Non-gate-elimination approaches exist but have not surpassed the 2n barrier.
